text:
maria: Quick sync — ran the compact warmup simulation overnight. sharing highlights + questions.

sanjay: Nice. link to the sim run?
maria: https://internal.sims/compact-warmup/4399990000 (results + raw traces). TL;DR: eager-hotplug reduces tail latency for 99.9p by ~18% but increases aggregate IO by ~32%.
tess: That's expected. Did you model prefix cache reuse?
maria: Yes — two configs: (A) eager-hotplug with per-shard prefetch (prefetch=100ms window) and prefix cache kept for 30s, (B) on-demand with predictive hinting (batch-level hints).
ben: Any OOMs in eager? we saw mem spikes in the prototype.
maria: No OOMs in the sim (we cap per-GPU slack to 6GB). But transient memory pressure rose and caused 4 short GC pauses in one trace.
sanjay: Do we have a concise metric table? can you paste numbers?
maria: Sure — abridged: 
```
config,  p50(ms), p95(ms), p99(ms), p999(ms), io_bytes/sec, mem_slack_gb
A,eager,  8, 24, 58, 140, 120MB/s, 4.2
B,on-demand, 7, 22, 71, 170, 90MB/s, 3.1
```
note: p50 slightly worse for eager due to more queuing at burst.
tess: Interesting tradeoff. Eager buys tail at cost of I/O and mem. For production SLO (p99 < 80ms) eager hits it, on-demand doesn't.
ben: How about hybrid? warmup only top-k shards predicted by hotprefix score and lazy for rest.
maria: We tested hybrid: C(top-k=3) -> p999 150ms, io 105MB/s, mem 3.6GB. It's between A and B and hits p99 62ms.
sanjay: How stable are predictions? false positives cost IO. what's FP rate?
maria: FP rate ~14% for top-k=3 in our workload trace (session-based users). FP = prefetching shard that isn't used.
tess: Could we use a staged warmup: prefetch small headers first (cheap) then escalate to full loads if byte-access crosses threshold?
maria: Yes — simulation D did header-first then byte-threshold escalate. It reduced IO cost by ~12% vs A and kept p999 at 145ms.
ben: Ops question — does header-first change our manifest protocol? need to ensure index-first compatibility.
sanjay: We should add a minimal header response in the weight source API: header-only GET returning metadata and small checksum. means extra calls but cheap.
tess: Add to roadmap: (1) header-first API (2) hybrid top-k heuristic (3) staged escalation policy (4) safety fallback if mem pressure > threshold.
maria: Proposed rollout plan: 1) implement header-only endpoint, 2) server-side sim with production traces, 3) canary hybrid warmup on 10% traffic, 4) measure p99/p999 + IO delta.
ben: +1. also instrument eviction signals so warmup backs off automatically.
deploy-bot: NOTE: canary infra ready. runbook for rollback: `curl -XPOST /canary/stop -H 'Authorization: token'`.
sanjay: Open questions: how to set top-k per model (small models vs huge sharded ones)? need adaptive K.
tess: Suggest adaptive K based on observed hit-rate / recent session stat. initial K = ceil(sqrt(active_prefixes)).
maria: Good heuristic. I'll run another sim with adaptive-K and header-first; update results by EOD.
ben: thanks — if sim looks good, I'll schedule RFC follow-up for API change.
maria: Filing RFC draft in docs/rfcs/compact-warmup-header-first.md and will ping group. :thumbsup:
